predictive_services_discussion: Hot and very dry conditions will persist for much of the Intermountain West. The Inland Northwest and northern Great Basin can expect temperatures near or above 100°F, while inland California will reach up to 110°F. Minimum RH will drop to 3-15% east of the Cascades and Sierra to the Continental Divide, with poor overnight recovery. Slight cooling is expected west of the Cascades. Above-normal temperatures will spread into much of the northern Rockies, as well. Temperatures will exceed 100°F in the lower elevations of the southern Great Basin, West Slope, and southern Plains. The southern Plains will also experience breezy south winds and RH minima between 20-30%. Conditions remain hotter and drier than normal in the Four Corners to northern New Mexico and southern Colorado. Isolated to scattered wet thunderstorms are forecast along and south of the Mogollon Rim and west of the Divide in New Mexico. Isolated mixed wet/dry thunderstorms capable of causing new ignitions are expected across far southern Nevada, southeast California, southwest Utah, northwest Arizona, and parts of the southern Plains. Alaska’s eastern interior remains warm and dry with isolated thunderstorms, raising the risk of new ignitions in the southeastern interior. The eastern U.S. will see near- seasonal temperatures, except for below-normal temperatures in the Southeast and well above-normal temperatures in Maine.
